cue_frames.caption_text: Training gives you a place to publish instructions, assign people, and
review their recorded progress.
We are on the New Training form in the fictional Chicago Fire department.
Enter Academy, Shared contact verification exercise as the Training name.
Use Description for a short explanation of what the training is about.
Here it says that this is practice finding and checking
fictional operational contacts.
A clear title and description help a member recognize the assignment
before opening the full lesson.
Training Text is the separate area for the instructions themselves.
Our exercise asks the learner to open Contacts, find Academy Partner
Directory, check the contact identity and current details, and
reopen an entry after an edit.
Read the complete paragraph before assigning it.
It gives someone a concrete task and a way to verify the result.
The wording also makes clear that the exercise does not authorize real outreach.
Keep the catalog description short and put the actual
learning steps in Training Text.
Set Minimum Score to one hundred percent for this one-question exercise
and choose November fifteenth, twenty twenty-six as its Due Date.
Review the audience before creating the training.
Add all Personnel is checked here, which selects the whole fictional department.
Groups To Add, Roles To Add, and Users To Add are the narrower alternatives
when you choose a smaller audience.
Do not assume a previously selected individual limits an assignment
while Add all Personnel is checked.
We will verify the resulting fourteen assignments after saving.
In Questions, use Add Question and enter: What should you do
after updating a shared contact?
Add two answers.
The first says to reopen the saved contact and verify the updated details.
The second says to assume the edit was saved without checking.
Mark the first answer as correct using its radio control.
Check the question, both answers, and the selected correct answer
before choosing Add Training.
One clear question is enough to demonstrate the difference
between assigning content and checking the learner’s response.
The new training appears in the catalog with its description and due date,
alongside the existing training entries.
Open Report for this training before completing the exercise.
The report separates Viewed, Completed, Score, and Result.
Boden’s initial row says Not Viewed, Not Completed, No Score, and Pending.
An assignment has been created, but that row does not yet record participation.
Use these separate columns to decide whether someone has opened
the training, submitted the quiz, or met the required score.
Open View Training for the saved exercise.
Check the title, due date, description, and full training
text from the learner’s side.
This training has a quiz, so opening its page records that it
was viewed; the learner still needs to answer and submit the quiz.
Take Quiz is a separate action in the right-hand panel.
Before taking it, review the instructions and any training files.
The learner view is a useful check that the content people receive
matches what you meant to assign.
Choose Take Quiz and
read the welcome stage.
Use Next to open Question One.
The same question and two answers from the training editor
now appear as learner choices.
Select the answer that says to reopen the saved contact and
verify the updated details.
The filled radio control shows the current choice.
Use Next to continue.
Selecting an answer is still preparation; a quiz result is
recorded after the learner submits it.
You can use Previous to review the question before finishing.
At the Finish stage, read the instruction to submit the quiz answers.
The Finish control at the lower right performs that submission; the Finish
label across the top identifies the stage.
Submit once and check the
returned catalog. For Boden, this exercise now shows Training Complete.
That is the completion indicator for the current learner.
Open Report to check the score and pass result as well, rather than
treating a completed submission as proof of the required score.
An administrator can add another handout after a learner has completed the quiz.
This training already lists the original contact-verification
file and quick-check dot txt.
On Edit, Existing Attachments identifies those saved files and Currently
Assigned still shows fourteen users.
Under Add Attachments, choose review dot txt.
Check the selected filename and use Save Training at the bottom of this form.
Reopen the learner view: Training files now lists all three handouts.
This completed learner has no Take Quiz panel here.
Verify the assignment count and
existing result separately
when maintaining a training.
After that edit, Report still shows Boden’s completed quiz,
score of one hundred, and Pass.
Viewed records the most recent opening, so its displayed time can
be later than the completion time.
The other thirteen assignments remain Pending.
Follow up with those learners separately.
Chicago Fire can use this workflow for a department software refresher.
Community care and mental health teams can assign operational process
learning; search and rescue can review support procedures; security teams can
teach site workflows; wildland crews can prepare seasonal information;
and industrial response teams can review facility coordination steps.
These recorded results describe this training and quiz;
professional qualifications belong in their own reviewed process.
